key_provisions_or_claims: AI robots should be given 'electronic person' legal personality as subjects of patent infringement.
Injunction responsibility lies with the robot itself, while financial compensation lies with the owner.
Amend Article 47 (penal provisions) of the Intelligent Robots Act to punish manufacturers and companies, with joint penal provisions.
Differentiate safety regulation by degree of human contact, with registration, inspection and licensing for high-contact robots.
Legislate user authentication and information security standards for remotely controlled robots.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Korean journal article proposing improvements to the Intelligent Robots Act. It argues for electronic personhood for AI robots in patent infringement, separating injunctive responsibility (robot) from compensation (owner), contact-based safety tiers, and new criminal penal provisions for manufacturers by amending Article 47.
annotation.title_clean: A Study on the Improvement of the Intelligent Robots Act
annotation.title_en: A Study on the Improvement of the Intelligent Robots Act
